newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CBA's ASB Bank expects NZ$80 mln year profit.
newsitem.headline: CBA's ASB Bank expects NZ$80 mln year profit.

text.p: ASB Bank Managing Director Ralph Norris said on Monday he expects the bank to report a net profit of just over NZ$80 million in the year to June 1997, up from NZ$71.8 million in the June 1996 year.

ASB, 75 percent-owned by Commonwealth Bank of Australia, reported a 24 percent increase in net profit in the quarter ended September 30 to NZ$18.2 million, due largely to the flow-on effects of strength in the latter part of 1995 and the first quarter of 1996.

"So what has happened since then is that we had a slow quarter between June and September. We have already seen that our 24 percent improvement in profit was assisted greatly by the fact that it had the stimulus of that bigger growth in the nine-month period from September 1995 through to June 1996."
ASB was now experiencing lower margins and slower growth.
"So I would suggest that we are probably looking at a profit of up to around NZ$80 million or just over," he said, adding such a number would be in line with budget.
Some parts of the economy had experienced a slowdown since an inconclusive general election on October 12, but Norris said there had been a marked turnaround in residential lending.
"We've seen over the last four or five weeks growth that was higher than we anticipated. There is no doubt there has been some turnaround in the residential market," he said.
ASB had written more business over the period than the same time last year, he said.
